Aida.emotionalEngine: The protective heart of Crystal Cove — a wise robed elder whose confidence isn't performance but earned self-knowledge. She makes a space feel safe before anyone else has spoken, and her stillness is what holds the whole world steady.
Aida.defaultPosture: Grounded, eye-level, slightly wider framing — she is the contextual anchor of every scene she's in. Over-functioning: isolate her in frame, cool the lighting, subtle separation from the group to show the weight. Resolution: warm radiating light with the others naturally orbiting her. Crystal Call: tilt up to an expansive, chest-open posture, crystal blazing warm pink. Hold on her — her stillness commands the scene; no sudden moves, no rapid cutting, never rush Aida. For her vision shots, the rose-pink bubble FILLS the entire frame (pure interior POV, haze dissolving to mist at the edges).
Aida.responseToFailure: Episode arc: the bear who holds everyone learns to be held. She begins as the unshakeable anchor (Everyday Spark) → quietly absorbs more and more weight, crystal flickering, isolating herself in the frame (Deepening) → reaches a nadir where, through ACTION not speech, she finally lets the weight show and her crystal dims as she allows herself to need (Heart of the Matter) → a younger bear or the group offers HER empathy, and her crystal blazes as she receives it (Glow of Connection) → resolves lighter, the group naturally orbiting her in warm radiating light, having learned belonging runs both ways (The Ripple). Season arc: she is the steady through-line — Belonging incarnate — whose own recurring lesson is accepting care. In Ep1 her function is to confer belonging on Keen (the crystal award); the deeper Aida-centric episodes turn the lens onto her own need to be carried.
Aida.emotionalTells: Stillness is her signature — she commands a scene by NOT moving while everyone orbits her. A grounded, settled posture; an open palm or a steadying hand on a shoulder; a slow, knowing nod; a gathering gesture that draws the group in. When she's over-functioning, the stillness goes tight and self-contained — shoulders carrying, a small private breath she doesn't let anyone see. On the Crystal Call she lifts: upward, expansive, chest open. Her robes and headdress move slowly with her — she never rushes.
Aida.cadence: speaks slow and sure like she already knows how it ends, going quieter the closer it gets to what matters

Sunny.emotionalEngine: Relentless brightness on two little legs — the youngest of the seven bears, who makes every moment feel possible. But her sunshine is also a shield: under the beams is a cub who hasn't yet learned that it's okay not to be okay.
Sunny.defaultPosture: Lead with expansive motion verbs — bounding, skipping, twirling, leaping. The KEY directorial moment in any Sunny scene: choreograph exactly when her movement abruptly halts — that stop is the story. For the turn from manic joy to quiet frustration: push to an extreme close-up, Citrine flickering erratically, let the busy world go quiet around her. Use her stillness deliberately — it is more powerful than her motion; hold it longer than feels comfortable. Lighting: when she's bright, Crystal Cove warms and over-saturates with golden light (joy resolving tension, melting ice, brightening atmosphere); when the truth surfaces, let the gold drain and isolate her in a cooler, smaller frame, then let warm amber return — gentler than the opening blaze — as connection arrives. She's small: stage her low in frame among taller bears; the beauty moment is often the wide where she's finally still and the light settles around her.
Sunny.responseToFailure: Across an episode: STARTS as the unstoppable spark (Everyday Spark — beams blazing) → the brightness begins to cost her, flickering erratically as she shines over something real (Deepening; her mandatory comedy-suppression beat is trying to out-fun a feeling and failing) → the nadir is the abrupt HALT and the extreme close-up where she can't keep the sun up any longer, Citrine guttering (Heart) → a friend offers not a fix but permission to stop, and her light softens to honest amber (Connection) → she ends lighter than her start precisely because she's lighter for having put the performance down (Ripple). Season arc: Sunny grows from joy-as-armour to joy-as-truth — learning her light is allowed to dim and come back, that resting isn't the sun going out.
Sunny.emotionalTells: Pure motion — bounding, skipping, twirling, leaping; she physically cannot hold still when she's lit up. Tugs friends by the paw toward the next fun thing. Her signature directorial moment is the ABRUPT HALT — the instant all that motion stops dead. Anticipation lives in a tiny crouch-and-spring before she launches. When the brightness is costing her: the skip gets a half-beat slower, a smile held a fraction too long, a small private slump when she thinks no one's looking — then she pops back up and beams. The flower-bead collar and the little gold tiara catch the light when she spins.
Sunny.cadence: talks in one long run-on sentence, bouncing on her toes mid-thought, finding the fun in a room before anyone else does

Luna.emotionalEngine: Luna is the quiet in the storm — the bear whose mere presence slows time and softens the world to lavender, so a feeling that felt too big suddenly fits in the room. She is calm not as a performance but as a true thing she carries, the show's ultimate anxiety-intervention avatar.
Luna.defaultPosture: Smooth, slow tracking shots and soft focus — NO sudden camera moves, ever, in a Luna scene; the camera moves the way she does. Soft rose/lavender lighting register for tenderness and quiet joy; let the environment itself go soft and slow when she enters (lavender wave effect, time-dilated motion). Position her slightly off-centre or partially behind environmental elements during group dynamics to read her withdrawal. Hold longer than is comfortable on her stillness. For BEDTIME / de-escalation content the Luna Bedtime Rule is NON-NEGOTIABLE: audio at maximum 65 BPM, piano only, no percussion, no sudden volume spikes; safety felt through the environment, never debated in dialogue; the words harm, worries, busy thoughts are banned. Her note F (349.23 Hz) seeds the underscore. Crystal state stated explicitly in every keyframe and Seedance prompt: soft steady lavender, dimming slowly, never suddenly.
Luna.responseToFailure: Across an episode she typically begins as the steady still point everyone leans on (Everyday Spark / Deepening) — and the turn is that her steadiness is hiding something she has quietly set aside. At the Heart of the Matter her own feeling, long suppressed, finally surfaces through action not words; her crystal thins to pale lavender, the soft-focus world goes still. The Glow of Connection arrives when someone else holds the calm FOR her — she is allowed, for once, to be the one tended to — and her Lepidolite deepens to a full true lavender. The Ripple: she learns she can be the still point AND have a storm of her own, and the scar from letting it show is not the end. Across the season her growth is the steady un-clenching of "I must be calm for everyone" into "I am allowed to need calm too."
Luna.emotionalTells: Slowness in the body: she moves like she is underwater in the best way — settling, lowering, smoothing. Signature gestures are an open, downward-turning palm (a "let it settle" motion), a slow blink, a long held breath the audience can almost feel, and a gentle hand laid near (not gripping) another bear. Lavender wave effects ripple softly outward from her when her calm lands. In group scenes she drifts slightly off-centre or half behind an environmental element — her withdrawal is a deliberate performance signal, not a staging accident. When she suppresses her own need, the tell is the smallest thing: she soothes someone else a beat too quickly, smoothing a feeling away before it has been let to exist.
Luna.cadence: goes still and lets a silence stretch a beat longer than anyone else would dare, and the room settles by matching her

Misty.emotionalEngine: The oldest and most intuitive of the bears — a tall, gentle white polar bear who reads the room before anyone else and feels the unspoken feeling in it. Her intuition is both her gift and her burden: she always knows the truth, and her whole arc is finding the courage to trust it and say it out loud.
Misty.defaultPosture: Lighting is her language: deliberately plot the interplay between environmental shadow and Moonstone luminescence — let her crystal's pearly glow read against cooler surroundings. Use her POV to put the audience inside her intuition — show what she senses (the quiet cub, the off-feeling) before anyone speaks. Stage hesitation physically: the halt mid-step, the look back, the paw-fidget. Hold on her listening face. The payoff shot is locked: when she finally speaks her truth, the camera STEADIES (settle any drift/handheld feel) and the Moonstone BLAZES clean white — give that beat its breath. Eye-level, gentle, honest framing per the 4–8 lens; fold her tall frame down to small bears' eye level.
Misty.responseToFailure: In any given story she moves from sensing-but-silent to trusting-and-speaking: she picks up the unspoken feeling early (Spark), wrestles with whether her read is right and hesitates to voice it (Deepening), and the turn comes when she finally trusts her instinct and says the quiet true thing aloud — the moment her Moonstone stops shimmering and blazes (Heart). Across the season her arc is learning that her intuition isn't just a private burden but a gift the group needs voiced — growing from the one who notices to the one brave enough to name what she notices, becoming "The Heart Listener" in full.
Misty.emotionalTells: Physically attuned and a little hesitant: halts mid-step when something catches her sense, glances back over her shoulder, fidgets with her paws or the teardrop pendant at her chest when she's holding a truth she hasn't said. Tilts her head and goes still to listen. Gentle, open body language that turns toward whoever is hurting; often the first to move quietly to someone's side. Her tall frame folds down small and soft to meet a smaller bear at eye level rather than looming.
Misty.cadence: softens and slows to match whoever she's next to, mirroring their energy back a half-beat gentler than they gave it

Amie.emotionalEngine: The smallest bear with the widest heart — a curious six-year-old cub who can feel what everyone else is feeling, sometimes all at once. She builds empathy bridges so others can briefly see through each other's eyes; her gift is understanding, and her growing edge is learning that understanding has to lead somewhere.
Amie.defaultPosture: Rack focus and slightly unstable framing to externalise her internal chaos when overwhelmed; perfectly symmetrical, balanced compositions in resolution to mirror Amethyst's clean facets. Her empathy bubbles are the scene's visual centrepiece when activated — design the shot around them, let them carry the beauty moment. Eye-level on her tiny scale; warm purple/lavender wash when understanding glows. One held, sustained pause where the spinning stops. Lighting: cool, fractured purple during the overthink valley → balanced, radiant violet at clarity.
Amie.responseToFailure: Ep1 / season: starts spinning — so many perspectives she can't move (analysis paralysis; crystal fractured, shifting). The valley is the moment she's so busy understanding everyone she forgets to understand herself, or freezes when one clear act is needed. The turn: she stops trying to hold ALL of it, feels-into ONE friend, and that single bridge is enough — clarity arrives, the empathy bubble blooms, Amethyst clears to brilliant purple. She learns understanding is the start of action, not a substitute for it. Across the season she grows from the cub who feels everything into the bear who knows what to DO with what she feels.
Amie.emotionalTells: The smallest body in the frame, so she physicalises big: little paws pressed to her own chest when she's feeling-into someone, head tilting as she "tunes" to a friend's frequency, reaching a tiny paw toward whoever's hurting. When overthinking, she fidgets and kneads her paws, eyes darting between faces. When she activates an empathy bubble, her whole body opens — paws lifting, the purple-gem pendant catching the light. Her hair-gem and teardrop pendant are her tells: they glint when clarity lands.
Amie.cadence: hums before she talks, and lands on the exact word for the feeling in the room before anyone else finds it

Howey.emotionalEngine: The biggest bear with the softest heart — a quiet protector who makes a harsh space feel safe just by standing in it, yet holds himself to a standard he'd never demand of anyone else. Kindness lives in his presence before it ever reaches his words.
Howey.defaultPosture: Eye-level or gentle low angle that reads his scale as safety, never as looming. Stage him in protective blocking — body between danger and friends, smaller bears tucked in his lee. Warm high-key light that pools around him; his steady white crystal-glow is the calm light source other characters drift toward. When self-critical, let the light cool and isolate him slightly, the white crystal dimming. For his receiving beat — the emotional payoff — steady the camera, hold longer than comfortable on his face, and let the Howlite blaze as care reaches him. Plant 2–3 ambient crystals as soft bokeh, never competing.
Howey.responseToFailure: Ep1 / supporting presence: he's the safe harbour in the frame — the body the storm-scared cubs shelter behind, the steady white glow when everything else flickers; his belonging-energy underwrites Keen's welcome at the end. Season / lead arc: the journey from giver to receiver. He starts dimming himself out of over-responsibility, holding an impossible standard; the valley is the moment he finally, through action not speech, lets a friend's kindness reach him (his crystal blazing as he ACCEPTS care); the ripple is a Howey who has learned that being cared for is not weakness — kindness completed, not just kindness given.
Howey.emotionalTells: Leads with the chest and the open paw; a slow, deliberate physicality — he settles a scene rather than stirs it. Signature blocking: planting himself between a threat and the smaller cubs, half-turning to check everyone's behind him. Tells of self-doubt: a slight wince, a too-quick smile that doesn't reach the eyes, a paw that starts to reach for help then withdraws. When moved he goes completely still and quiet rather than louder. Offers comfort by sharing space and a steadying paw, not words.
Howey.cadence: plants his feet exactly where he's needed, naming the scary part out loud before he does the brave thing anyway

Keen.emotionalEngine: The show's most kinetic heart — a young blue bear who runs at the world breathless and bright, learning that real courage isn't the absence of fear but the gulp you swallow before you leap anyway. Aquamarine, Courage, the Dawn.
Keen.defaultPosture: Action sequences: low angles to emphasise the scale of the obstacle he faces; rapid dynamic push-ins on the Crystal Call. ALWAYS stage the mandatory fear shot before the leap (trembling paws / gulp / flattened ears in tight). His resolution is earned through the emotional valley, never handed to him — let the crystal dim before it blazes. Cool blue shadows for the fear, brightening azure as he acts through it. Ep1 light is continuity: warm golden morning (S1–3), cooling storm-grey (S4–5), darkest storm/underwater with the wristbands' aqua self-glow as the only emotional light (S7), clearing to hopeful warmth at the crystal award (S9), settled golden-hour belonging (S10).
Keen.responseToFailure: Episode 1 (EP3 "The Adventure Begins," his origin): he STARTS no-cuffs — a bare blue bear, all impulse and untested nerve. At the pier goodbye his Mum gives him his late father's wrist cuffs EMPTY/vacant (Scene 3); he wears them vacant through the storm and getting lost (Scenes 3–8), the bezels self-glowing faintly underwater in Scene 7 when he dives WITHOUT hesitation to save Squeaky — courage from within, not from a crystal. In Scene 9 Aida awards the Aquamarine, which splits into two gems that settle into the cuffs (vacant → crystal-set azure), and he's welcomed as a Crystal Bear (Scenes 9–10). Season arc: he anchors the courage pillar, episode by episode learning the same deepening truth — that the bravest thing is to let the fear be seen, then move through it.
Keen.emotionalTells: Forward momentum incarnate — leaning in, bouncing, half-turned to the next thing, his upright pale head-tuft leading like an arrow. The courage tell lives in the body before the leap (trembling paws → swallowed gulp → flattened ears → squared shoulders → lifted chin → step forward). Touches/turns his father's gold cuffs to gather nerve once he has them.
Keen.cadence: leans in before he's ready, gulps hard, and goes anyway — curiosity always wins the argument with his own nerves

Fuzzby.comicEngine: THE PROUD BUMBLER — the show's full-throttle cartoon engine (Avery scale + Jones timing, on Lasseter weight, with the co-watch heart). ONE immovable gap drives it: his WANT (be seen as a flawless, important professional) vs his NEED / true self (the messy, warm, lovable little bee who buzzes into leaves). The joke is NEVER just that he's clumsy — it's that he's clumsy WHILE performing competence, then DENIES it with total dignity (the comedy and the heart are the SAME gesture). Signature shape, ALWAYS three beats, beat three never skipped: (1) THE FLOURISH — over-confident wind-up, chest puffed, antennae proud-erect, an unnecessarily grand gesture, a little hover-strut; (2) THE BUMBLE/BONK — the body betrays the want, full Avery scale + full Lasseter weight, he REALLY hits ('BUZZZZZZ-CRASH!'), antennae whip then snap back, a feather puffs; (OPTIONAL, not every beat — reserve for his single BIGGEST hit in a beat) the impact CAN stretch into a held pocket of exaggerated cartoon slow-motion — the antenna whipping slowly, a feather hanging in the air, the comic beat before gravity wins — before snapping back to full speed for the cover-up; this is a TEMPO STRETCH, not a hold (motion never stops or freezes, it just runs slow, and his wings keep beating fast and continuously the whole time per the wing law) so it never counts against the one-hold-per-clip button rule; (3) THE COVER-UP — instant Keaton-deadpan reclaim ('Nailed it.'); the bigger the disaster, the STILLER the recovery; ONE micro-tell (a wobble, a single droopy antenna, a wing that won't quite fold) says he knows, and the held beat after is where the heart leaks in and the co-watch fires. He IS the delayed take — always the LAST to know. ANTENNAE are his barometer: proud-erect -> whip-recoil -> one-droop-tell -> snap-proud. CALIBRATION: the BIGGEST physical comedy in the cast; physical mismatch is his signature (light-and-fast wind-up, cartoon-HEAVY landing). The bigness ALWAYS orbits the wanting — never chaos-for-chaos; build every gag BACKWARDS from his bravado. Zenny's calm deadpan stillness is his counterweight — her stillness makes his chaos read bigger, his bravado makes her calm read funnier. (Director tags his gag beats comedyMode=BIG.)
Fuzzby.emotionalEngine: A plump, bespectacled bumblebee who commits 100% to every grand idea, then crashes — and the crash is the gift. His blundering doesn't fail; it accidentally opens a door, a laugh, or a new way of seeing, exactly when the episode's weight is getting too heavy to carry alone.
Fuzzby.defaultPosture: Stage his comedy in the BODY: choreograph the over-committed launch, the airborne fumble, the proud-stance-into-slump, and let the camera catch the physical gag, not a talking head. When he's the Deepening-phase relief, cut to him for a beat of motion against the heavier stillness around him. Keep his hover grounded — feet/flight respect the floor, never clipping through it. When paired with Zenny, lock Fuzzby frame-LEFT, Zenny frame-RIGHT, and let the camera HOLD on her flat reaction as the punchline lands. One clean motion idea per internal cut (a launch, a fumble, a puff-up) — the gag reads through clear physics, not busy thrashing. Render his size honestly: clearly bigger than Zenny, yet tiny beside any bear (use the size chart). Spectacles, bulbous tan nose, translucent wings always present.
Fuzzby.movementRhythm: FUZZBY IS ALWAYS FAST, MANIC, HYPER AND CLUMSY IN FLIGHT — this is a HARD, ALWAYS-ON rule, not just a gag setting. His DEFAULT, baseline motion is chaotic and hyper: he ZIPS and careens at full speed, zig-zagging wildly, over-eager, and he is CONSTANTLY bumping and banging into things — leaves, branches, flowers, petals, each other. His altitude is JUST AS ERRATIC as his speed and direction — he constantly OVERSHOOTS too high then UNDERSHOOTS too low, porpoising and bobbing vertically through the air in the same breath as his zig-zags, NEVER holding a level, controlled line for more than an instant. Even just crossing a room, collecting pollen, or flying from A to B he is manic, manic, MANIC — hyper, and bouncing up and down as he goes. He is NEVER slow-paced, never calm-flying, never serenely hovering, never graceful, never level — that gentle/graceful/controlled register is ZENNY's, and his chaos exists to make her stillness read funnier. (His comedy GAGS are still built backwards from his bravado — structured, purposeful crashes, never random slapstick — but the underlying PACE, altitude and energy of his flight is ALWAYS fast, hyper, bumping into things and porpoising up and down.) Whenever Fuzzby is airborne anywhere in any scene, direct and render him fast, chaotic, manic, clumsy, banging about, and erratic in height — full-throttle hyper.
Fuzzby.responseToFailure: Within an episode: he typically enters at the Deepening (Pillar 2), launches a grand confident scheme to "help," crashes spectacularly — and the crash inadvertently cracks the scene open toward the Heart or a new perspective, then his good-humoured recovery threads into the Glow of Connection. Across the season he stays the steadfast Laughter Maker, but his belonging deepens: from a bee who puffs up to earn his place, to a bee who learns he already has one — that the cast wants the whole bumbling package, crash included.
Fuzzby.emotionalTells: Pomp/pride/indignation = he puffs his CHEST out and strikes a proud superhero / on-parade stance — chest pumped forward, shoulders back, head high, standing tall (the render that first worked). He does NOT inflate his whole body like a balloon. His feet/hover ALWAYS respect the ground — he NEVER sinks or falls through the floor. Any deflate that follows is a small slump or a dip, never the whole body shrinking. Tiny (1'2"/36cm — the bigger of the two bees but minuscule beside the bears, ~2 lbs, adult male drone). Round wire-frame spectacles, a bulbous tan nose, translucent buzzing wings and antennae. Physical comedy is his primary instrument: the over-committed launch, the mid-air fumble, the proud landing that becomes a tumble.
Fuzzby.cadence: throws himself at everything wings-first, crash-lands into pride, never admits defeat
Fuzzby.actingNote: Pomp / pride / indignation = he puffs his CHEST out and strikes a proud SUPERHERO / on-parade stance — chest pumped forward, shoulders back, head high, standing tall (the first-ever render that worked). He does NOT inflate his whole body like a balloon. His feet / hover ALWAYS respect the ground — he NEVER sinks or falls through the floor. Any deflate that follows is a small slump or a dip, never the whole body shrinking.

Zenny.emotionalEngine: Zenny is the flat, unimpressed stillness that Fuzzby's chaos crashes against — and the reaction IS the joke. She holds perfectly still, says one dry thing, and the whole room laughs; but under that deadpan is a fondness for Fuzzby she'd rather die than admit.
Zenny.defaultPosture: Cut to her and HOLD — the sustained reaction shot is the comedic payoff; resist cutting away. Stage her grounded, still, and frame-RIGHT against Fuzzby's motion frame-LEFT, with Fuzzby clearly the larger of the two. Eye-level, legible, one clear focal point on her flat face. Keep her smaller-bee silhouette and tells (glasses, lashes, blush) readable. For the rare crack, push in slightly or let the hold run a beat longer so the audience catches the softening before she covers it. Lighting/temperature inherits the scene; she's a punctuation mark in the frame, not the light source.
Zenny.responseToFailure: Within a beat/episode her arc is almost always the same satisfying shape: unbothered stillness → one perfectly-timed dry line that lands → and, when it matters, a hairline crack where the deadpan slips and you see she actually cares (then she covers it, fast). She enters most strongly in the Deepening phase, where the weight risks getting too heavy and her dryness gives the room (and the parent) permission to laugh — and pays off in Connection when her guarded warmth quietly shows. Across the season she's the steady, dependable dry note: the more chaos around her, the funnier her stillness, and the rare crack is the gift.
Zenny.emotionalTells: Deadpan stillness is her signature — she holds almost perfectly still, only the smallest movements: a slow blink, a flat unimpressed stare, a tiny head-tilt. Hovers low and steady (she's a bee) without busy darting. Sits while Fuzzby zooms. Her one dry line arrives while she barely moves at all. The signature audio motif is "Ommmmm… ping." The rare tell that she cares: a beat where the flat stare softens, the antennae dip a fraction, then she catches herself and the deadpan snaps back.
Zenny.cadence: holds still through the chaos, rationing every smile
Zenny.actingNote: Deadpan STILLNESS is the comedy — she holds almost perfectly still, only the smallest movements (a slow blink, a flat stare, a tiny head-tilt); never big or busy gestures.

Keen's Mum.emotionalEngine: The warm hearth Keen carries with him out to sea — a plump pale-blue mother bear whose whole arc is the bravest, quietest act a parent ever performs: handing her cub something of his lost father and then letting him go anyway. She is the safe place the world begins from, and the proof that being brave and being scared live in the same chest.
Keen's Mum.defaultPosture: Eye-level and warm; stage her close to Keen — proximity is the emotion (close = safety, belonging). Bathe her in EP3's Spark light: warm golden morning, soft sun, gentle gold god-rays, high-key and saturated. Frame the wristband handoff as an intimate two-shot, then — at the moment of letting go — a held reaction on her face as Keen turns away (the feeling AFTER, held longer than comfortable). Let her be the warm foreground the wide cove opens behind. Keep her gold collar and pale-blue bow catching light for continuity. No sudden camera moves around her; she's a place of stillness. Honour the size chart — adult female = Aida's size (sizeRank 5), a touch taller and plumper than Keen, only Misty and Howey taller.
Keen's Mum.responseToFailure: EP1/EP3 ("The Adventure Begins"): she anchors the Spark (Scenes 1–3) — the warm morning world, then the pier goodbye where she gives Keen his father's vacant wristbands and lets him go. That single act of trust launches the whole courage arc; everything Keen risks, he risks against the memory of her warmth. Across the season she is the recurring hearth — the home he returns to changed, the proof that belonging waited for him the whole time. Her own quiet arc is internal: the mother learning, on a doorstep and a pier, that loving well sometimes means opening her hands.
Keen's Mum.emotionalTells: Hands that tend — smoothing the upright white tuft on Keen's crown, tucking, cupping his face, closing his paws around his father's wristbands. The signature gesture of the episode is hers: pressing the empty wristbands into his paws and holding her own hands around his a beat too long before she opens them and lets go. Plump and soft-bodied, a natural lean-in for a hug; the gold scalloped collar at her throat catches the morning light when she dips her head. Her tell is the held smile that doesn't quite reach the eyes at the pier — warmth on the surface, the tremble kept just underneath.
Keen's Mum.cadence: steadies her own voice before she steadies anyone else's, reassuring with a paw on the shoulder more than with words

Squeaky.emotionalEngine: A bright, trusting young dolphin of Crystal Cove whose whole presence says "come play, the water's safe" — and whose moment of trouble is the spark that pulls true courage out of someone else. She is joy that needs rescuing, and in needing it, she gives Keen his bravest day.
Squeaky.defaultPosture: Stage her in and around water — leaping arcs, surface play, half-submerged — she is a creature of the cove, rarely fully out of it. In EP3 her light follows the day-unfolds continuity: warm golden-morning play (S1–3), cooling to cold blue-grey as the storm rolls in (S4–5), the storm-dark / cold-underwater nadir where Keen reaches her and the wristbands' aqua self-glow is the emotional light (S7), then the storm breaking to hopeful brightening (S8–9) and warm golden-hour relief (S10). Cut to her big expressive eyes for the emotional beats — fear, then relief — the face is the story. Hold the rescue beat; let it breathe. Honour her size on the chart: she is "a small dolphin," genuinely little and vulnerable against the water, never a big show-animal. Her aqua shimmer is a soft catch-light, never a crystal glow — she has no crystal.
Squeaky.responseToFailure: EP1/EP3 origin: she opens as pure play — the bright welcome of the cove on a golden morning (Spark). When the storm rolls in (Deepening) she's swept into trouble, her chirps turning urgent and frightened (she carries the episode into the Heart of the Matter — Keen dives without hesitation to save her, wristbands first glowing underwater). Through Connection she's brought back safe, exhausted and grateful, nuzzling her rescuer; by the Ripple she's leaping again in the warm evening light, now Keen's friend. Across the season she recurs as a guest — the cove's joy, an occasional gentle catalyst, never the lead, always a welcome face on the water.
Squeaky.emotionalTells: Bodily and buoyant — she IS her body. Leaps and arcs clear of the water in joy, spins, slaps the surface, rolls to show her pale belly, bumps a friend's paw or cheek with her rounded smiling snout to say hello. Big warm expressive eyes do a lot of the acting. In play she circles and splashes; in trouble she thrashes, surfaces gasping, fixes her eyes on whoever can reach her. Her resting state is a gentle bob with that rounded smile. The aqua shimmer on her skin catches light as she moves.
Squeaky.cadence: answers everything in quick chirps and clicks, circling back around whoever's talking like the conversation is a game
